label: EU(7)-PIM: pethidine
title: Pethidine in an older person
statement: Pethidine (also called meperidine) is a medicine to avoid in older people. It raises the risk of falls, fractures, confusion, dependency and withdrawal. The 2015 list suggests a low starting dose, a short course and dose reduction in renal impairment. Australian DBL pethidine product information rules out continuous intravenous infusion and patient-controlled analgesia in people with renal impairment.

plain_summary: Pethidine is a strong opioid pain medicine. In people aged 65 and over it can cause confusion, falls and dependency, and safer pain medicines exist.

medicine_groups.name: Pethidine
medicine_groups.note: Also written meperidine. Australian supply is as an injection, so the history shows the ingredient name, often with a company name. No brand is listed.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when pethidine (meperidine) is supplied to a person aged 65 or over. If pethidine is supplied and age is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is aged 65 or over. One supply is enough.
cannot_be_seen: Why pethidine was needed (for example palliative care or a short hospital stay), kidney function, and how much pethidine was actually given or taken. Also medicines given in hospital or by another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether pethidine is still needed and whether a safer pain medicine could replace it.
